cohort: The study included 264 women with confirmed Cesarean scar pregnancy and 295 women who underwent elective termination (control group).
finding: Systemic immune-inflammation indices (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were significantly higher in women with Cesarean scar pregnancy, with NLR demonstrating predictive value for CSP.
cross-section timing: Blood counts were analyzed at the time of diagnosis of Cesarean scar pregnancy or at the time of elective termination for the control group.
